entries.title: Psalms 91:1
segments:
The present is the first of ten anonymous psalms which seem to belong to the same age.  They are all of a joyous character, anticipating, in the language of faith and hope, the triumph of God's people over all evil.  Their general character gives them a peculiar adaptation to the public worship of God in all ages. 
 
The change of persons in the psalm now before us is remarkable.  The writer announces as his theme the safety of the believer who dwells under God's protection,
; he speaks of himself as such a believer,

, God addresses the believer. 
 
  Secret place of the Most High; his pavilion, in which he hides his friends from all harm.

.  We dwell in the secret place of the Most High by faith in him and habitual communion with him. 
 
Habitual access to God is a source of perpetual and perfect security.

entries.title: Psalms 91:3
segments: The snare of the fowler; the plots of crafty foes.

entries.title: Psalms 91:5
segments:
Terror; danger that causes terror. 
 
  By night--by day; they whom God protects shall be safe from every danger. 
 
From the numerous evils by night and by day to which the wicked are exposed, those who trust in the Lord shall be delivered.

entries.title: Psalms 91:7
segments: A thousand--ten thousand; a definite for an indefinite number.

entries.title: Psalms 91:9
segments: Because thou hast made--habitation; this verse may be literally rendered thus: "For thou, Lord, art my refuge; thou hast made the Most High thy habitation."  As in
, he first speaks of himself as a believer, and then addresses the believer.  We make the Lord our dwelling-place, by habitually resorting to him for comfort and protection.

entries.title: Psalms 91:10
segments: There shall no evil befall thee; this promise is not inconsistent with the chastisement wherewith God visits his people for their profit, that they may be "partakers of his holiness;" this, though for the present "not joyous, but grievous," is no evil, but a rich blessing.

entries.title: Psalms 91:11
segments: To the heirs of salvation, angels are ministering spirits; in the path of duty God will protect them from all evil, or sanctify his dispensations to their highest good.

entries.title: Psalms 91:12
segments: Dash; stumble by striking.  To be kept from stumbling, is to be kept in the way of truth and safety.
These words contain no promise of protection when we tempt God by needlessly exposing ourselves to danger.

entries.title: Psalms 91:13
segments:
Tread upon; overcome. 
 
  Lion--adder--young lion--dragon; enemies of all classes, the strong and the subtle, the fierce and the malignant.

entries.title: Psalms 91:14
segments: Known my name; been acquainted with my character, and confided in my care.

entries.title: Psalms 91:15
segments: God's people are not exempt from trouble; but the have his promise that in all their trials he will be with them and deliver them and make them partakers of his everlasting salvation.
